title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.8932: the fused pass 1 with checkpoint compares every 20th round, R = 2^24, kappa = 1.0001

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.8932 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on the published 4ac17b66 package (125.8933: R = 2^24, h = 0.00005, p0 = 0.3900503 and kappa = 1.0001 from its shipped hazard census, unchanged) and through it on 4c8222cc, cbea87bf and the fused-arrival chain; the fused pass 1 is kept, with one change: the checkpoint is compared only in rounds t = 0 (mod 20). Those rounds run pass1f (129.03125 per walk); the others run pass1p, the same macro without the K_cp load and the filter compare (127.03125). Anchors move to rounds t = 0 (mod 5120), so a cycle of length L <= 256 is compared at its anchored class lcm(L, 20) <= 5060 rounds later, before the next anchor; the anchor cap is 16*2^52 periods (16*2^52*5120 = 20*2^64 = L_max). The pseudocode's length test is the model; production uses the anchor counter, so no per-arrival test is added; the walk's classes, escapes and endpoints are unchanged and the waste bound w <= 2^-14.257 stays inside the 2^-14.25 the kappa rule allows (certificate.py asserts the coverage, w and both kappa bounds). The 256-per-walk reserve is a separate word only the 20/25 stub charges debit; reports, starts, fallbacks and traversals charge the general remainder, so none can consume it. Step 571.5713; compare rounds' 2 per walk, anchors' 14 and writes are hard rows; traversal is step + 39. The declared run executes both fused copies (548 walks, 0 mismatches); all 600 toy starts reach the same endpoint (proof.md 5.2). Declared dependencies: 4ac17b66 (direct base), cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 0a1c5772; the rest are transitive through 4ac17b66. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory <2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units, charged; nonuniform advice zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995074, phase 1 = 2^125.892513, hard extras = 2^113.474375, random extras = 2^99.8052, allowance = 2^114.092911, W_ledger = 2^125.8931810 < 2^125.8932; Markov ratio 0.0000477532 < 0.00005; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1258932 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1258931 exactly. No prior acceptance or score is a premise; this is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 20th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (with rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub), both copies of the fused pass 1, emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
